name: Assegno Unico Universale - SIA Project 24 25
description:
The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian
    Assegno Unico Universale (AUU), a financial benefit provided by INPS to
    families with dependent children. The considered scenario focuses exclusively
    on applications submitted directly by interested users through the INPS website,
    excluding applications submitted by delegated patronage institutions, mobile
    applications, and call-center interactions.

    An authenticated applicant can submit an AUU application as a parent,
    foster parent, or legal guardian of a child. During the first phase of the
    application, the applicant provides information about each dependent child,
    including the child's fiscal code, dependency status, disability status and,
    when applicable, disability level. Depending on the applicant type, additional
    information concerning family composition, exclusive custody, the other
    parent's fiscal code, and the requested allowance distribution between parents
    must also be provided.

    When a child's fiscal code is entered, the system verifies it in real time.
    If the child is already associated with another active application, the
    application flow is blocked and an explanatory warning is shown. The applicant
    may also specify adult dependent children who do not directly qualify for AUU
    but contribute to determining household composition. Duplicate fiscal codes for
    adult children are detected and reported.

    The amount of the allowance depends on the applicant's economic situation.
    If INPS does not already possess a valid ISEE when the application is submitted,
    the minimum allowance established by regulation is used. If a valid ISEE becomes
    available later, INPS automatically recalculates the allowance without requiring
    the applicant to modify the application.

    In the payment phase, the applicant specifies the payment method. If the
    allowance is to be divided equally between both parents, the payment information
    of the other parent must also be provided. Supported payment methods include
    credit to a SEPA IBAN account owned by the beneficiary, domiciled payment at a
    post office, and credit to an eligible prepaid card.

    Before submitting the application, the applicant must read and accept the
    declarations of responsibility and the GDPR privacy notice. The system then
    presents a summary of the entered information so that it can be reviewed.
    If validation errors are detected, the application is not submitted and the
    applicant must correct the erroneous information. If validation succeeds, the
    application is submitted and a receipt can be downloaded.

    An application may be interrupted without saving or saved as a draft before
    submission. A saved draft can later be consulted and completed. When resuming
    a draft, the applicant may either continue from the previously saved information
    or discard it and restart the application from the beginning.

    Once submitted, the application is evaluated by authorized INPS staff.
    The application may be accepted, rejected because the applicant is not entitled
    to the benefit, or suspended when additional documentation is required.
    The applicant is notified of the outcome. An accepted application remains valid
    for twelve months and the corresponding allowance is paid automatically every
    month.

    When an application is suspended, the INPS operator specifies which additional
    documents are required. The applicant can consult the application, upload the
    requested attachments, reconfirm the application data, and again accept the
    responsibility declarations and privacy notice.

    The system also allows an application originally submitted by one parent to be
    completed by the other parent. The other parent can consult the application and
    confirm or modify the proposed allowance distribution. If the applicant requested
    the entire allowance, the other parent may accept the 100 percent allocation or
    request a 50 percent distribution. When payment to the other parent is required,
    that parent provides their own payment information.

    Applicants can also add one or more children to an existing application.
    Each new child's fiscal code is checked in real time to ensure that the child
    is not already associated with another active application. After adding the
    child, existing payment and declaration data can be confirmed or modified.

    Finally, the system provides supporting functions that allow citizens to consult
    previously submitted applications, consult general information about the
    Assegno Unico Universale, and simulate the expected monthly allowance amount.

highLevelGoals: The applicant aims to successfully submit an application for the Assegno Unico Universale benefit online through the INPS website.
The applicant seeks to provide all necessary and accurate information regarding dependent children, family composition, and other required details for the AUU application.
The applicant desires to specify and manage the preferred payment method for the allowance, including providing details for the other parent if the allowance is to be divided.
The applicant needs to review all entered information, accept declarations of responsibility and privacy notice, and ensure data accuracy before final submission.
The applicant aims to save an incomplete application as a draft and later resume it to complete the submission process.
The applicant expects to be notified of the evaluation outcome of their submitted application (accepted, rejected, or suspended) and to consult its status.
The applicant needs to upload requested additional documents for suspended applications to facilitate their evaluation.
The applicant aims to add new children to an existing application and confirm or modify associated payment and declaration data.
The other parent aims to consult an AUU application originally submitted by the primary applicant.
The other parent seeks to confirm or modify the proposed distribution of the allowance, including accepting a 100% allocation or requesting a 50% distribution.
The other parent needs to provide their own payment information if they are to receive a portion of the allowance.
The citizen aims to consult general information and guidelines regarding the Assegno Unico Universale benefit.
The citizen desires to simulate the expected monthly allowance amount based on provided criteria.
The INPS Staff/Operator aims to evaluate submitted AUU applications to determine eligibility and correctness.
The INPS Staff/Operator needs to accept, reject, or suspend applications based on evaluation results and specify reasons or required documentation.

The INPS staff member marks an application as approved after successful evaluation.
The INPS staff member marks an application as denied and specifies the grounds for rejection.

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actors are accurate and cover the main roles described in the text. However, the distinction between "Applicant" and "Citizen" is somewhat redundant, as an applicant is also a citizen who can perform the supporting functions (consulting info, simulating allowance). It would be more precise to either merge them into a single "Citizen/Applicant" actor or clarify that "Citizen" refers to non-applicants using the simulation tools. Additionally, while "INPS Staff/Operator" is correctly identified, the description could be more specific about their actions (e.g., requesting documents, evaluating). Overall, the set is representative, but the separation of Applicant and Citizen is a minor conceptual overlap.

branch_005.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Save and Resume Application Drafts' is directly supported by the project description, which states: 'An application may be interrupted without saving or saved as a draft before submission. A saved draft can later be consulted and completed.' The goal accurately captures the applicant's intention to manage the lifecycle of an incomplete application across multiple sessions. It is distinct from 'Submit AUU Application' (which focuses on the final act of submission) and 'Modify Existing Application' (which refers to adding children to an already submitted or active application, not resuming a draft). The scope is appropriate and the wording is clear. This is a material omission of an essential capability defined in the parent HLG's scope.

The text explicitly states that 'The applicant is notified of the outcome' (accepted, rejected, or suspended) and that the system allows citizens to 'consult previously submitted applications'. The bottom-up reconstruction confirms this intention. The scope is appropriate, distinguishing it from the submission phase (covered by 'Submit AUU Application') and the specific action of providing documents for suspended cases (covered by 'Provide Additional Documentation'). While 'Provide Additional Documentation' is a reactive action triggered by a status, the overarching goal of monitoring the status and receiving the final outcome remains distinct and valid. There is no semantic overlap with other HLGs that would necessitate removal or rewriting. The parent HLG 'Monitor Application Status and Outcome' requires the applicant to be notified of the evaluation outcome and to consult the status. The current LLGs cover: (1) retrieving current status (llg_001), (2) viewing evaluation outcome details including reasons (llg_002), and (3) viewing notifications/alerts regarding status changes (llg_003). These three goals collectively satisfy the requirement to 'consult its status' and 'be notified of the evaluation outcome'. The documentation states 'The applicant is notified of the outcome' and 'The applicant can consult the application'. The decomposition is complete and does not duplicate capabilities from sibling HLGs (e.g., 'Provide Additional Documentation' handles the upload action, while this HLG handles the monitoring/notification aspect). No essential capabilities are missing, and no LLGs are contradicted by the documentation.

branch_007.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Provide Additional Documentation' is supported by the project description, which states that when an application is suspended, the applicant can upload requested attachments. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Applicant provides requested documentation to resolve a suspended application' captures the same functional intention and scope. The original goal is reasonably scoped to the specific action of providing documentation for suspended applications, which is distinct from other goals like 'Monitor Application Status' (which covers notification/consultation) or 'Modify Existing Application' (which covers adding children). There is no semantic overlap that would necessitate removal, and the original wording is sufficiently clear and faithful to the requirements. Therefore, it should be kept. The parent HLG 'Provide Additional Documentation' is grounded in the documentation section: 'When an application is suspended, the INPS operator specifies which additional documents are required. The applicant can consult the application, upload the requested attachments, reconfirm the application data, and again accept the responsibility declarations and privacy notice.' The current LLGs cover 'viewing the list of required documents' (consulting the application/requirements) and 'uploading an additional document'. While the documentation mentions 'reconfirm the application data' and 'accept declarations', these actions are typically part of the final submission/confirmation workflow which is often handled by a broader 'Submit' or 'Review' HLG, or considered part of the finalization of the upload process. However, looking closely at the sibling HLGs, 'Review and Confirm Application' exists for the initial submission. For a suspended application, the specific act of providing the documentation is the core of this HLG. The two LLGs capture the essential interaction: knowing what is needed and providing it. The 'reconfirm' and 'accept declarations' steps are closely tied to the act of resubmitting the application with the new docs. Given the instruction to be conservative and that 'Technical/API wording alone is not an error' and 'Different granularity... are not material defects', the current LLGs adequately decompose the primary user intent of providing the documentation. The missing steps (reconfirm/accept) are arguably part of the final submission action which might be implicit in the completion of the upload flow or handled by a generic submission mechanism not explicitly broken out as a separate HLG for this specific suspended state in the provided list (though 'Submit AUU Application' is a sibling, it usually refers to the initial submission). However, even if 'reconfirm' is missing, is it an *essential capability explicitly required by the parent HLG*? The parent HLG is 'Provide Additional Documentation'. The core capability is providing the docs. The reconfirmation is a procedural step to finalize. Without a specific sibling HLG for 'Resubmit Suspended Application', one might argue it's missing. But looking at the sibling 'Submit AUU Application', it describes the initial submission. The documentation says 'upload... reconfirm... accept'. If the LLGs only cover view and upload, the 'reconfirm/accept' is missing. Is it essential to 'Provide Additional Documentation'? Yes, because the application isn't resolved just by uploading; it requires the re-acceptance. However, often in these decompositions, 'Upload' implies the transaction that includes the necessary confirmations, or the 'Submit' HLG is reused. Let's look at the sibling 'Review and Confirm Application'. It says 'before final submission'. This suggests it's for the initial flow. There is no sibling for 'Resubmit'. Therefore, the capability to 'Reconfirm data and accept declarations' for the suspended application is likely essential to resolving it. Is it covered? No. Is it essential? The documentation explicitly lists it as a step the applicant takes when the application is suspended. 'The applicant can consult the application, upload the requested attachments, reconfirm the application data, and again accept the responsibility declarations and privacy notice.' All four are listed as capabilities the applicant can perform in this state. The current LLGs only cover the first two (consult/view and upload). The last two (reconfirm and accept) are missing. Are they essential to the HLG 'Provide Additional Documentation'? The HLG name is specific to documentation, but the description says 'to facilitate their evaluation'. The evaluation cannot proceed without the reconfirmation/acceptance. Thus, these are essential capabilities of the workflow described in the HLG's context. However, the prompt asks to decide conservatively. Is 'reconfirm' a distinct capability from 'upload'? In many systems, uploading a file and submitting the form are separate. If the LLG 'Upload' is just the file transfer, the submission/reconfirmation is missing. Given the explicit documentation listing these as distinct actions ('upload... reconfirm... accept'), and the absence of a sibling HLG covering the resubmission/confirmation of a suspended application, these capabilities are missing from the current LLGs. Therefore, regeneration is warranted to include the reconfirmation and acceptance steps, or to clarify that the upload LLG encompasses the final submission of the suspended application package. Since the current LLGs are atomic ('views list', 'uploads document'), they do not cover the 'reconfirm' and 'accept' steps. These are essential to the resolution of the suspension. Thus, REGENERATE.

The current LLGs cover 'viewing the list of required documents' (consulting the application/requirements) and 'uploading an additional document'. While the documentation mentions 'reconfirm the application data' and 'accept declarations', these actions are typically part of the final submission/confirmation workflow which is often handled by a broader 'Submit' or 'Review' HLG, or considered part of the finalization of the upload process. However, looking closely at the sibling HLGs, 'Review and Confirm Application' exists for the initial submission. For a suspended application, the specific act of providing the documentation is the core of this HLG. The two LLGs capture the essential interaction: knowing what is needed and providing it. The 'reconfirm' and 'accept declarations' steps are closely tied to the act of resubmitting the application with the new docs. Given the instruction to be conservative and that 'Technical/API wording alone is not an error' and 'Different granularity... are not material defects', the current LLGs adequately decompose the primary user intent of providing the documentation. The missing steps (reconfirm/accept) are arguably part of the final submission action which might be implicit in the completion of the upload flow or handled by a generic submission mechanism not explicitly broken out as a separate HLG for this specific suspended state in the provided list (though 'Submit AUU Application' is a sibling, it usually refers to the initial submission). However, even if 'reconfirm' is missing, is it an *essential capability explicitly required by the parent HLG*? The parent HLG is 'Provide Additional Documentation'. The core capability is providing the docs. The reconfirmation is a procedural step to finalize. Without a specific sibling HLG for 'Resubmit Suspended Application', one might argue it's missing. But looking at the sibling 'Submit AUU Application', it describes the initial submission. The documentation says 'upload... reconfirm... accept'. If the LLGs only cover view and upload, the 'reconfirm/accept' is missing. Is it essential to 'Provide Additional Documentation'? Yes, because the application isn't resolved just by uploading; it requires the re-acceptance. However, often in these decompositions, 'Upload' implies the transaction that includes the necessary confirmations, or the 'Submit' HLG is reused. Let's look at the sibling 'Review and Confirm Application'. It says 'before final submission'. This suggests it's for the initial flow. There is no sibling for 'Resubmit'. Therefore, the capability to 'Reconfirm data and accept declarations' for the suspended application is likely essential to resolving it. Is it covered? No. Is it essential? The documentation explicitly lists it as a step the applicant takes when the application is suspended. 'The applicant can consult the application, upload the requested attachments, reconfirm the application data, and again accept the responsibility declarations and privacy notice.' All four are listed as capabilities the applicant can perform in this state. The current LLGs only cover the first two (consult/view and upload). The last two (reconfirm and accept) are missing. Are they essential to the HLG 'Provide Additional Documentation'? The HLG name is specific to documentation, but the description says 'to facilitate their evaluation'. The evaluation cannot proceed without the reconfirmation/acceptance. Thus, these are essential capabilities of the workflow described in the HLG's context. However, the prompt asks to decide conservatively. Is 'reconfirm' a distinct capability from 'upload'? In many systems, uploading a file and submitting the form are separate. If the LLG 'Upload' is just the file transfer, the submission/reconfirmation is missing. Given the explicit documentation listing these as distinct actions ('upload... reconfirm... accept'), and the absence of a sibling HLG covering the resubmission/confirmation of a suspended application, these capabilities are missing from the current LLGs. Therefore, regeneration is warranted to include the reconfirmation and acceptance steps, or to clarify that the upload LLG encompasses the final submission of the suspended application package. Since the current LLGs are atomic ('views list', 'uploads document'), they do not cover the 'reconfirm' and 'accept' steps. These are essential to the resolution of the suspension. Thus, REGENERATE.

In Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering, it is generally preferred to have a single high-level goal for the core activity (Evaluation) that encompasses the decision-making process, rather than splitting it into 'Evaluate' and 'Manage Outcomes' which are tightly coupled and sequential parts of the same workflow. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Application Evaluation Status' suggests a focus on state management, but the core intent is the decision-making process. Since 'Evaluate AUU Applications' already covers the actor's intention to process the application and determine its fate, keeping 'Manage Application Outcomes' as a separate HLG creates redundancy. The decision to accept, reject, or suspend is the direct output of the evaluation. Therefore, the original goal should be removed to avoid splitting one stakeholder intention into wording variants or closely related sub-goals that are already covered by the broader 'Evaluate' goal.

The role of the 'Other Parent' in consulting, confirming distribution, and providing payment details is covered by 'Consult Shared Application', 'Confirm Allowance Distribution', and 'Provide Personal Payment Information'. The supporting functions for citizens (consulting info and simulating amounts) are covered by 'Access General AUU Information' and 'Simulate Allowance Amount'. The INPS staff actions of evaluating and managing outcomes are covered by 'Evaluate AUU Applications' and 'Manage Application Outcomes'. No distinct, documented functional intention remains uncovered.

The bottom-up reconstruction aligns with this intent. While there is some semantic overlap with 'Provide Accurate Application Data' (which covers family composition and distribution requests), the specific focus on the *payment mechanism* and *disbursement details* distinguishes this goal sufficiently to warrant keeping it as a distinct functional intention, especially given the specific constraints and options for payment methods described in the text. It is not too generic, narrow, or incorrectly scoped. The current low-level goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Configure Allowance Payment and Distribution'. 
1. **Distribution**: llg_001 covers the selection of the distribution method (100% vs split), and llg_002 covers the provision of co-beneficiary identification details, which is explicitly required by the documentation ('the payment information of the other parent must also be provided' implies identification is needed to link the payment). 
2. **Payment Methods**: llg_003 covers the selection of the payment instrument type. llg_004, llg_005, and llg_006 cover the specific data entry for the three supported methods: SEPA IBAN, Post Office, and Prepaid Card. 
3. **Scope Check**: The HLG is specifically about the *applicant* configuring the payment and distribution. The sibling HLGs 'Confirm Allowance Distribution' and 'Provide Personal Payment Information' belong to the *Other Parent* actor and are correctly excluded from this branch. The sibling HLG 'Modify Existing Application' covers adding children and modifying data later, which is a distinct lifecycle event from the initial configuration. 
4. **Completeness**: All essential capabilities defined in the HLG description ('specifying the payment method and, if applicable, providing co-beneficiary details') are present. There are no contradictions with the documentation. The granularity is appropriate for API-mappable goals.

However, there is significant semantic overlap with the existing High-Level Goal 'Submit AUU Application'. The act of reviewing and confirming is the final, mandatory step of the submission process. Keeping them as separate high-level goals splits a single stakeholder intention (submitting the application) into two closely related steps. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Applicant to Confirm and Commit to Application Submission' highlights that this is about the final commitment. Given the instruction to remove HLGs when another HLG for the same actor already covers the same functional intention (or when they merely split one intention), and considering 'Submit AUU Application' is the broader goal that encompasses the final validation and acceptance steps, this specific HLG is redundant. The 'Submit AUU Application' goal inherently includes the requirement to validate and accept terms before the submission is successful. Therefore, it should be removed to avoid redundancy.

branch_005.rationale: The project description explicitly states: 'An application may be interrupted without saving or saved as a draft before submission. A saved draft can later be consulted and completed.' This directly supports the intention of the Applicant to save and resume incomplete applications. The original High-Level Goal 'Save and Resume Application Drafts' accurately captures this functional intention. It is distinct from 'Submit AUU Application' (which focuses on the final submission) and 'Modify Existing Application' (which focuses on adding children to an already submitted or active application, not resuming a draft). The scope is appropriate and the actor is correct. The parent HLG 'Save and Resume Application Drafts' requires the applicant to save an incomplete application, retrieve a list of such drafts, and select one to continue. The current LLGs cover these three core capabilities: saving (llg_001), retrieving the list (llg_002), and loading/continuing a specific draft (llg_003). The documentation mentions that when resuming, the applicant may discard the draft and restart. However, 'discarding' is a destructive operation often considered part of draft management, but the core intent of 'resuming' is to continue. The current LLGs capture the essential flow of saving, listing, and resuming. The capability to 'discard' is not explicitly required by the HLG description ('save... and later resume it to complete'), though it is in the text. Even if 'discard' is considered, it is a sub-operation of managing the draft state, and the primary goal of resuming is covered. More importantly, the HLG description focuses on saving and resuming to complete. The current LLGs are atomic, API-mappable, and cover the necessary lifecycle steps for the stated goal. There are no contradictions with the documentation. The sibling HLGs do not cover draft management. Therefore, the decomposition is complete and correct.

branch_007.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Provide Additional Documentation' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that when an application is suspended, the applicant can upload requested attachments. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Applicant provides requested documentation to resolve a suspended application' captures the same functional intention and scope. The original goal is reasonably scoped to the specific context of suspended applications and does not overlap with other goals like 'Submit AUU Application' (initial submission) or 'Modify Existing Application' (adding children). Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The parent HLG 'Provide Additional Documentation' is grounded in the documentation section: 'When an application is suspended, the INPS operator specifies which additional documents are required. The applicant can consult the application, upload the requested attachments, reconfirm the application data, and again accept the responsibility declarations and privacy notice.' The current LLGs cover 'viewing the list of required documents' (llg_001) and 'uploading an additional document' (llg_002). While the documentation mentions 'reconfirm the application data' and 'accept the responsibility declarations', these actions are typically associated with the final submission or modification steps. However, in the context of resolving a suspension, the core capability is providing the missing documents. The sibling HLG 'Review and Confirm Application' covers the general review/acceptance flow for initial submission. The sibling 'Modify Existing Application' covers adding children. The specific act of 'reconfirming data' after uploading documents might be considered part of the submission of the additional documentation package. However, looking closely at the prompt's instruction: 'Decide conservatively... Regenerate only when at least one essential capability explicitly required by the parent HLG is absent'. The parent HLG description is 'The applicant needs to upload requested additional documents...'. The LLGs cover viewing the requirements and uploading the documents. The 'reconfirmation' and 'acceptance of declarations' are procedural steps that often accompany the submission of the documents. Are they essential capabilities of *this* HLG or part of a broader 'Submit/Resubmit' flow? The documentation says 'upload the requested attachments, reconfirm the application data, and again accept...'. This implies a sequence. If the HLG is strictly 'Provide Additional Documentation', the upload is the key action. The viewing is necessary to know what to provide. The reconfirmation/acceptance might be seen as part of the 'Submit' action which is a sibling or a subsequent step. However, often in these systems, the 'Provide Documentation' HLG encompasses the entire interaction to resolve the suspension. Let's look at the sibling 'Review and Confirm Application'. It says 'before final submission'. The suspension resolution is a re-submission. If the LLGs do not include the confirmation/acceptance step, is that a material defect? The prompt says 'Do not regenerate for... merely possible improvements'. Is the confirmation step 'essential' to the HLG 'Provide Additional Documentation'? The HLG name is specific. The description says 'upload requested additional documents'. It does not explicitly say 'and confirm data'. The documentation links them. However, if we look at the sibling 'Modify Existing Application', it involves confirming/modifying data. The suspension flow is distinct. If the applicant uploads documents but doesn't confirm/accept, the process isn't complete. But is that capability *owned* by this HLG? The HLG is 'Provide Additional Documentation'. The act of providing is the upload. The confirmation is a validation step. Given the conservative instruction and the fact that the core 'provision' of documents is covered by viewing and uploading, and the confirmation steps are often generic submission mechanics, I will lean towards KEEP. The LLGs are atomic and map to the core intent. The 'reconfirmation' might be considered part of the 'Submit' action which is not explicitly a sibling HLG for the *suspension* context, but 'Review and Confirm' is a sibling. If 'Review and Confirm' is a sibling, does it cover the suspension case? Its description says 'before final submission'. The suspension case is a re-submission. It's ambiguous. However, the primary goal 'Provide Additional Documentation' is satisfied by the ability to see what is needed and upload it. The confirmation is a system requirement for the transaction to close, but the *user goal* is to provide the docs. I will keep the LLGs as they capture the essential user-facing actions for the specific goal of providing the docs.

branch_015.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Manage Application Outcomes' is supported by the project description, which states that INPS staff evaluate applications and may accept, reject, or suspend them, specifying reasons or required documentation. However, there is a significant semantic overlap with the existing High-Level Goal 'Evaluate AUU Applications' for the same actor. The existing goal 'Evaluate AUU Applications' describes the process of determining eligibility and correctness, which inherently leads to the outcomes (accept/reject/suspend). The original goal focuses on the *result* of that evaluation. In Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering, it is generally preferred to have a single high-level goal for the core functional process (Evaluation) that encompasses the decision-making, rather than splitting it into 'Evaluate' and 'Manage Outcomes' which are tightly coupled and describe the same stakeholder intention from slightly different angles (process vs. result). The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Application Evaluation Status' suggests a focus on state management, but the core intent is the evaluation decision. Since 'Evaluate AUU Applications' already covers the actor's primary responsibility of processing the application to a final state, keeping 'Manage Application Outcomes' as a separate HLG creates redundancy. The intention is better captured by the existing 'Evaluate AUU Applications' goal, or the original goal should be removed to avoid splitting one stakeholder intention into wording variants. Given the instruction to remove when another HLG covers the same functional intention, and 'Evaluate' is the broader functional intent that includes the outcome determination, the original goal is redundant.

branch_009.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Provide Personal Payment Information' is supported by the project description, which states: 'When payment to the other parent is required, that parent provides their own payment information.' However, looking at the existing High-Level Goals for the 'Other Parent' actor, we have 'Consult Shared Application' and 'Confirm Allowance Distribution'. The action of providing payment information is a specific step that occurs *after* or *during* the confirmation of the distribution if the other parent is to receive funds. While distinct from 'Confirm Allowance Distribution' (which is about the percentage split), it is a very narrow, transactional step. More importantly, the bottom-up reconstruction suggests 'Manage Allowance Distribution to Other Parent'. However, 'Manage Allowance Distribution' is semantically very close to the existing 'Confirm Allowance Distribution'. The existing 'Confirm Allowance Distribution' goal description says: 'confirm or modify the proposed distribution...'. Providing payment info is a prerequisite or part of finalizing that distribution for the other parent. Is it a separate intention? The project description groups these actions: 'The other parent can consult the application and confirm or modify the proposed allowance distribution... When payment to the other parent is required, that parent provides their own payment information.' These are closely linked. However, 'Provide Personal Payment Information' is a distinct functional requirement from 'Confirm Distribution' (which is about the split). But is it a high-level goal? It is a specific task. Let's look at the 'Applicant' goals. The Applicant has 'Configure Allowance Payment and Distribution'. The Other Parent's equivalent is confirming the distribution and providing their payment details. If we keep 'Provide Personal Payment Information', it is a valid, supported intention. Is it too narrow? It is a specific action. But in Goal-Oriented RE, high-level goals should represent significant user intentions. 'Providing payment info' is a means to an end (receiving the allowance). The end is 'Receive Allowance' or 'Finalize Participation'. The existing 'Confirm Allowance Distribution' covers the decision on the split. The payment info is the execution detail. Often, these are grouped. However, the prompt asks to judge if it should be kept, rewritten, or removed. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Allowance Distribution to Other Parent' is broader and potentially overlaps with 'Confirm Allowance Distribution'. If I rewrite to 'Manage Allowance Distribution', it might overlap with the existing 'Confirm Allowance Distribution'. If I keep 'Provide Personal Payment Information', it is precise and supported. Is it a 'High-Level' goal? It is a specific task. But for the Other Parent, their interaction is limited. They consult, confirm distribution, and provide payment info. These are the three main steps. 'Consult' is covered. 'Confirm Distribution' is covered. 'Provide Payment Info' is the remaining distinct functional block. Therefore, it is a valid, distinct intention from 'Confirm Distribution' (which is about the *amount/percentage*) and 'Consult' (which is about *viewing*). It is not generic. It is not incorrectly scoped. It is supported. Thus, it should be kept. The parent HLG 'Provide Personal Payment Information' explicitly states that the other parent needs to provide their own payment information if they are to receive a portion of the allowance. The documentation specifies that supported payment methods include credit to a SEPA IBAN account, domiciled payment at a post office, and credit to an eligible prepaid card. The current LLG (llg_001) is titled 'Other parent provides their bank account details for allowance payment' and described as inputting 'banking information'. This is a material defect because it restricts the capability to only bank accounts (IBAN), excluding the other explicitly supported methods (post office and prepaid card) which are essential to the general requirement of providing 'payment information'. Therefore, the decomposition is incomplete and misleading regarding the scope of acceptable payment methods.

branch_009.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Provide Personal Payment Information' is supported by the project description, which states: 'When payment to the other parent is required, that parent provides their own payment information.' The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage allowance payment reception details for the other parent' is semantically equivalent but slightly more generic. The original goal is specific, correctly scoped to the 'Other Parent' actor, and distinct from the 'Applicant's' goal to 'Configure Allowance Payment and Distribution' (which focuses on the primary applicant's setup). There is no overlap with other 'Other Parent' goals ('Consult Shared Application', 'Confirm Allowance Distribution'). Therefore, the original goal is faithful and should be kept. The parent HLG 'Provide Personal Payment Information' requires the other parent to provide their own payment information if they are to receive a portion of the allowance. The documentation explicitly lists three supported payment methods: credit to a SEPA IBAN account, domiciled payment at a post office, and credit to an eligible prepaid card. The current LLGs (llg_001, llg_002, llg_003) accurately decompose this requirement into these three specific methods. There are no missing essential capabilities, and no LLGs are contradicted by the documentation. The decomposition is complete and correct.
